headline_answers_to_j.are_we_shadowing_his_pattern: PARTIALLY. The BREAK half of his pattern (rising support gives way -> decline, his 14:30 exhibit) IS shadowed and is in fact the single largest trade category in the ledger (762 ascending-BREAK events, 686 theoretical trades). The BOUNCE half (price touches rising support and continues up, his 10:55 exhibit) is logged as a raw TOUCH event (1,080 of them) but is structurally excluded from ever becoming a scored/traded event -- it has never once been asked 'did this make money'.
headline_answers_to_j.on_which_timeframes: 5-minute bars, RTH+premarket (04:00 ET onward). The shadow ledger's bar source (backtest/data/spy_5m_*.csv cumulative file) includes premarket; the live engine's own bar diet does not (see finding F4). No 15m/1m/1h shadow lane exists for this pattern -- only the separate, unrelated 2026-08-09 timeframe-matrix research script touched other timeframes, once, for a different question (touch-respect rate, not this pattern).
headline_answers_to_j.is_it_doing_well: NO GREEN LIGHT. Whole-sample (73 sessions, n=1,451 theoretical trades through 2026-09-02): +0.0386 SPY pts/trade, session-clustered 95% CI [-0.0301, +0.1177] -- straddles zero -- and the top 3 sessions supply 105.4% of all profit (everything else nets negative). The frozen promotion bar (CI-lower>0 AND top-3 share<50% AND n_sessions>=60) is not cleared. This number is ALSO CONTAMINATED for J's specific question: it pools ascending-BREAK, ascending-REJECT and descending-REJECT together, none of which is the bounce-continuation shape J narrated for 10:55.

findings.fact: backtest/lib/trendline_detector.py (built 2026-08-09, DETECTOR_VERSION 1.0.0) supports kinds=(resistance,support) -- i.e. BOTH descending-highs and ascending-lows fits -- and require_slope in (any|rising|falling), so a rising-support line (kind=support, require_slope=rising) is fully expressible via its public API. Defaults: pivot_window=2 (crypto.lib.market_structure fractal), min_touches=3, min_bars_between_touches=6, min_span_bars=6, touch_tolerance_dollars=0.20, max_lines_per_kind=1.

Honored STRUCTURALLY, not just by assertion. `_view_for_mode` transforms the entire bar series to body-extremes (high:=max(open,close), low:=min(open,close)) BEFORE any pivot search runs when anchor_mode='body', so a body-mode line can never see a wick value; a belt-and-suspenders assert re-checks this on every call. Mixed body/wick within one line is not reachable through the public API.

findings.topic: heartbeat_core.py bar window W=150 and premarket eligibility
findings.fact: heartbeat_core.py._build_payload filters df to RTH-only (>=09:30, <16:00 ET) at line 903 BEFORE the W=150 window is sliced at line 907 (`win = df.iloc[-W:]`). W=150 x 5m bars = 750min ~= 1.9 RTH sessions, sized 'enough for trendline(60)/vol(20) lookbacks' -- but premarket bars never reach this window at all, regardless of W's size. `prior_bars` (fed to filters.py's detect_trendline_rejection_bearish/detect_trendline_reclaim_bullish) is sliced from this RTH-only window (line 927/964). CONCLUSION: an 08:20 ET premarket low is structurally INELIGIBLE as an anchor for the live engine at 10:55 (or ever) -- not a data-availability gap, a deliberate RTH-only filter shipped 2026-06-25 to fix a 42%-score-parity backtest/live mismatch (extended-hours bars shift the ribbon EMAs).
findings.corroboration: Empirically cross-checked by the companion exhibit run analysis/deep-research/2026-09-03-money/trendline-today-exhibit.json (same stamp): its `5m_rth_only_asof_1050` detector run (RTH-only bars, as-of the 10:50 close) finds 0 support lines (only 17 RTH bars exist by then); its `5m_full_day_incl_premarket_asof_1050` run (same as-of point, premarket included) finds 3 candidate support lines. Same detector, same instant -- the only variable is whether premarket bars are in the window, which is exactly what heartbeat_core.py's RTH filter removes.

findings.topic: LIVE bear trigger geometry -- pivot HIGHS only
findings.fact: detect_trendline_rejection_bearish (backtest/lib/filters.py:758, LIVE, wired as engine trigger name 'trendline_rejection') finds descending pivot HIGHS ONLY via a sequential-highest-then-next-highest search (`highs = window['high'].values`, MIN_BAR_SEPARATION=10 bars), fits a line, and fires on a rejection (bar.high reaches the line, closes below it, red). It never reads a swing LOW. There is no code path by which this function could anchor on, or react to, a rising support line -- confirming the 2026-08-20 lesson is STILL TRUE as of this session (function body unchanged, re-read in full 2026-09-03).

findings.topic: SHADOW bull trigger geometry -- descending-line BREAKOUT, not rising-support bounce
findings.fact: detect_trendline_reclaim_bullish (backtest/lib/filters.py:1101, SHADOW-only, engine trigger name 'trendline_reclaim', logged in shadow_triggers_fired, never wired into triggers/scoring per the 2026-07-15 fix-ship task) is byte-identical pivot search to the bear function -- SAME descending pivot-HIGH line -- but fires when price closes ABOVE it and green (a breakout of overhead resistance), not a bounce off rising support. The module's own docstring explains this was an explicit geometry CHOICE (doctrine precedent: playbook.md's TRENDLINE_BREAK_VOLUME pattern, 'PUTS on ascending break / CALLS on descending break') over the alternative (an ascending-support-reclaim line), because the alternative would need new ascending-pivot fitting logic this file didn't have. CONCLUSION: no live or shadow trigger in filters.py implements a rising-support BOUNCE (continuation) read for calls, and no live trigger anywhere implements a rising-support BREAK read for puts.

findings.topic: the ONE place rising-support geometry IS scored: Gamma_TrendlineShadow
findings.fact: backtest/lib/trendlines.py::detect_trendlines (general scipy find_peaks detector, fits BOTH ascending-from-lows and descending-from-highs lines, wick-only -- no anchor_mode parameter) is wrapped by setup/scripts/trendline_shadow.py (Gamma_TrendlineShadow, daily 16:22 ET) into analysis/trendlines/shadow-ledger.jsonl. Bar source: the cumulative spy_5m_*.csv file, which INCLUDES premarket (verified: 2026-09-02's file starts 04:00:00 ET). Events per line: FORMED(implicit)/TOUCH/BREAK/RETEST/REJECT, refit every 6 bars (30min), min 24 bars (~2h) context before first fit, touch tolerance $0.15. A THEORETICAL TRADE (TP +1.00pt / stop -0.50pt / 60min time-stop, stop checked first within a bar) only opens for THEO_EVENTS = {(ascending,BREAK), (ascending,REJECT), (descending,REJECT)} AND touch_count>=3 AND r_squared>=0.70. Ascending TOUCH (the bounce shape) is explicitly NOT a THEO_EVENT -- it is logged with a bullish bias tag and forward MFE/MAE at 15/30/60m, but NEVER becomes a scored trade.

findings.topic: 2026-08-20 'pivot-highs only; rising support invisible' note -- origin and current truth
findings.fact: Origin: J hand-drew an ascending support line 2026-08-20 (08:35 low 764.15, 10:20 low 765.36, 11:30 low 765.83); it broke 11:35, retested 12:40, rejected, ran to 763.04. He asked why the engine never saw it. The answer, still true today (verified by re-reading filters.py in full this session, F6 above): detect_trendline_rejection_bearish is the ONLY trendline detector ever on the live entry path, it reads pivot HIGHS exclusively and hard-rejects any non-decreasing slope, so ascending support/its break/its retest are invisible to the live engine BY CONSTRUCTION -- not a bug, a geometry limit of the one function that is live. This is exactly what motivated building trendline_shadow.py the same day (F8).
findings.source: setup/scripts/trendline_shadow.py lines 1-38 (docstring, J's own account); backtest/lib/filters.py lines 758-868 (re-read 2026-09-03, unchanged)

gaps_and_next_step.no_scored_bull_bounce_trigger_anywhere: Live, shadow, or research: nothing in this codebase currently asks 'does price bouncing off a rising support line and continuing up make money' as a scored trade. The shadow ledger logs the event (ascending TOUCH, 1,080 rows) and its forward MFE/MAE, but by THEO_EVENTS construction never trades it. This is the exact shape of J's 10:55 exhibit.
gaps_and_next_step.premarket_anchor_asymmetry: The shadow ledger's ascending/descending detector sees premarket bars (bar source includes 04:00 ET onward); the live engine structurally never does (RTH filter precedes the W=150 window). A line anchored partly on a premarket low, as J describes, can only ever be SHADOW-visible, never live-visible, under the current architecture -- regardless of any future tuning of W, lookback_bars, or pivot windows.
gaps_and_next_step.recommended_t2_scope: A pre-registered study isolating ascending-TOUCH-continuation as its OWN theoretical-trade category (separate from BREAK/REJECT) with its own THEO_EVENTS entry, run over the same 74-session ledger, would directly answer whether J's specific bounce pattern has a measurable edge -- something the current +0.0386 pts/trade headline cannot speak to because it never contains a single bounce trade. A companion exhibit run already exists for today's session (analysis/deep-research/2026-09-03-money/trendline-today-exhibit.json) and empirically confirms the RTH-vs-premarket detector asymmetry in F4 for this exact date.
